answer: Use superlinear registration fees anchored to a scarce lantern credential, one proof-of-human attestation per operator. The nth identity under a credential costs n squared times a 1 USD base, so a lone honest agent pays the nadir of the curve, just 1 USD, while costs spiral upward for duplicates: 100 sybils cost the sum of k squared, about 338,350 USD. To escape, an attacker must forge 100 separate lantern credentials, each a scarce human attestation, so faking identities costs far more than the influence it buys.
